quickstart.title: Quick Start (Onboarding)
quickstart.description: Step-by-step unboxing and onboarding guide to get your Zenso frame up and running.
quickstart.intro: Setting up your Zenso frame requires zero coding and takes less than two minutes.
quickstart.step1_desc: Turn on the power switch located on the rear panel. The e-paper display will cycle through an initial waveform wipe and present the onboarding screen.
quickstart.step2_desc:
On your smartphone, open your Wi-Fi settings:
1. Connect to the temporary hotspot broadcast by the frame (SSID: `Zenso-Setup`).
2. A captive portal will appear automatically.
3. Select your home 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network and enter your network password.
   *(Note: 5 GHz-only bands are not supported by the 802.11 b/g/n radio).*
quickstart.step3_desc: Once connected to the internet, the frame fetches device authorization and displays an authentic pairing QR code on its 7.3" screen. Scan it with any smartphone camera to open the Zenso management portal.
quickstart.step4_desc:
In the portal, pick what to display:
- **Family Photo Albums**: Personal memories and curated artwork with automatic orientation and e-ink color dithering.
- **Ambient Weather**: Live conditions, forecasts, and barometric trends.
- **Calendar & Agenda**: Google Calendar or CalDAV events.
- **Bento Grids**: Multi-widget layouts configured without writing a line of code.
quickstart.step5_desc: Your frame will update quietly according to your preferred schedule (e.g., hourly during the day, asleep overnight) and immediately enter ultra-low power deep sleep (< 15 µA) between refreshes, preserving battery and home tranquility.

overview.title: System Architecture & Rendering
overview.description: How Zenso renders widgets in the cloud or local server and streams dithered buffers to low-power e-paper frames.
overview.intro: Unlike typical tablets or digital photo frames that run power-hungry operating systems, local web browsers, and backlights, Zenso utilizes an efficient **server-side rendering pipeline**. The frame remains in deep sleep mode and only wakes for brief seconds to check for updates.
overview.flow_content:
Widget Data & Templates
  → Liquid Template Engine (Modular Widgets)
  → Headless Render Pipeline (High-DPI Chromium with Cairo)
  → Color Quantization & Dithering (ACeP 7-Color Palette)
  → 4bpp RAW Bitmap Compression
  → Secure delivery over Wi-Fi
  → Frame draws to e-paper & enters deep sleep (< 15 µA)
overview.etag_desc:
When the device wakes on its scheduled timer, it issues an HTTP conditional request sending the `ETag` of its currently cached `/display.raw` buffer. If the layout or widget data has not changed:
1. The server immediately returns an empty `HTTP 304 Not Modified` header.
2. The frame skips display refresh entirely.
3. The microcontroller returns to deep sleep in less than a second, saving battery.
overview.refresh_desc: Refresh intervals can be tailored in the management portal to suit your daily rhythm (e.g., refresh weather hourly between 07:00 and 22:00, and sleep completely overnight).
overview.local_desc: Zenso displays are engineered for complete privacy. You can use the official Zenso Cloud, or run your own lightweight Docker container stack on your home network with zero telemetry and no cloud dependency.

faq.title: Non-Technical FAQ & Daily Experience
faq.description: Frequently asked questions about battery life, light emission, Wi-Fi networks, and everyday usage.
faq.q1: Does the frame emit light in the bedroom or at night?
faq.a1:
**No, absolutely none.**

Zenso uses reflective electronic paper with physical color pigment microcapsules. It produces zero backlight, zero blue light, and zero glare, looking just like museum-grade archival paper print under ambient room lighting. At night when the room lights are off, the frame is completely dark.
faq.q2: What happens when the battery runs out?
faq.a2:
**The image stays on the screen forever.**

The ACeP e-paper technology is bi-stable. This means the micro-pigments stay locked in position indefinitely with zero electrical power. The last displayed image or family photo remains crisp and visible forever until you plug in a standard USB-C charger.
faq.a3:
**Standard 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n networks.**

Zenso connects to standard 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (supported by virtually all home broadband routers). 5 GHz-only bands are not supported by the hardware radio. If your home Wi-Fi broadcasts separate SSID names for 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz, connect to the 2.4 GHz network during initial onboarding.
faq.q4: Can multiple family members send photos to the frame?
faq.a4:
**Yes.**

You can share your frame's private invite link or pairing QR code with trusted family members through [panel.zenso.ink](https://panel.zenso.ink) so they can contribute photos to your shared album without needing technical knowledge.
